name: Sinaloa Crow
rangeDescription: Coastal lowlands of western mexico (southern sonora to western nayarit)
description: Small glossy crow, common in northwest Mexico; endemic. Occurs in towns, villages, rubbish dumps, farmland, and semiopen areas with hedges and taller trees; often near water.

name: Subtropical Doradito
rangeDescription: Andes of colombia to northwestern argentina (south to la rioja)
description: A bright flycatcher found in marshes in the Andes from Colombia to Argentina. Yellow below and olive above, sometimes showing a hint of a dark mask and dull yellowish edges on the wing feathers.

name: Morningbird
rangeDescription: Palau (babelthuap to peleliu)
description: A rather small, mostly drab passerine. Male has a brownish-olive body with a darker hood and chest and a thick dark bill.

name: Greater Yellow-headed Vulture
rangeDescription: The guianas and southern venezuela to northern bolivia and northern brazil
description: Widespread and common vulture in lowland rainforest. Head may not appear yellow unless seen at close range.

name: Kosrae White-eye
rangeDescription: Kosrae (eastern caroline islands)
description: Small ash-gray warbler-like bird, endemic to the Micronesian island of Kosrae. Combination of uniform coloration, size, and pale eye-ring makes this species unique on the island.

name: Zanzibar Red Bishop
rangeDescription: Southeastern kenya to eastern tanzania, zanzibar, pemba, and northern mozambique
description: Breeding males are spectacular birds with completely black underparts and mostly orange-red upperparts. Females and non-breeding males are brown and streaky.

name: Gray Hawk
rangeDescription: Lowlands of southwestern usa to northwestern costa rica
description: Compact raptor. Adults distinctive, all pale gray with thin white bars on underparts.

name: Swainson's Hawk
rangeDescription: Western north america; winters to northern argentina, southern brazil, and paraguay
description: Longer-winged than Red-tailed Hawk, but otherwise the same size. Found in prairies and agricultural regions of western U.S.

name: Violet Turaco
rangeDescription: Southern senegambia to northwestern cameroon, southern chad, and central african republic
description: Spectacular purple turaco with a beautiful facial pattern: a large red-and-yellow bill, red bare skin around the eye, a white patch behind the eye, and a dark red back of the head. Shows large crimson wing patches in flight.

name: Yellow-legged Pigeon
rangeDescription: Bismarck archipelago and solomon islands
description: Body is mostly iridescent green below and dark blue above and on the wings, with diagnostic bright yellow legs and a bright silver head with pinkish yellow-tipped bill. Most often seen in flight in small flocks over forest canopy at dusk and dawn, where flocking behavior and combination of silver head and bright yellow legs are diagnostic.

name: Tawny Tit-Spinetail
rangeDescription: Locally in andes of central and southeastern peru, bolivia, and northwestern argentina (jujuy, salta)
description: Small, bright cinnamon bird with a long tail. Found at high elevations in pockets of short Polylepis forests and scrub, usually surrounded by grasslands or barren rock.

name: Wrinkled Hornbill
rangeDescription: Malay peninsula, sumatra, and borneo
description: Brightly-colored medium-large hornbill. Both sexes are black with bare facial skin, blobby throat “pouches”, yellowish tails, and casqued bills.

name: Golden-chevroned Tanager
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil (southern bahia to eastern minas gerais and santa catarina)
description: Large blue and yellow tanager with a thinner bill than other similar species. Males are mostly blue with yellowish edges to the wing feathers and tail.

name: Yellow-crested Helmetshrike
rangeDescription: Montane forest of east-central democratic republic of the congo and (?) adjacent southwestern uganda
description: A distinctive black helmetshrike with a bright yellow crown and crest, orange eye-rings, and pink legs and feet. A rare and threatened species restricted to four locations in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, found in pairs and small groups at middle levels and in the canopy of Albertine Rift montane forest.

name: Palau Scops-Owl
rangeDescription: Lowlands of palau (western caroline islands)
description: A reddish-brown owl with a large rounded head, pale whitish eyebrows, and no ear tufts. Upperparts spotted with black-tipped white spots.

name: Vermilion Cardinal
rangeDescription: Caribbean littoral of northeastern colombia and northern venezuela including isla margarita
description: A garish scarlet bird sporting a dramatic spiky crest and a hefty gray bill. Male overall brilliant red with black chin; female brown, gray-headed, with red crest and tail.

name: White-throated Hummingbird
rangeDescription: Eastern bolivia to eastern paraguay, northern argentina, and southeastern brazil
description: Very distinctive humminbird; both sexes have mossy green bodies and bold white throats and bellies. The bill is bicolored with a red lower mandible.

name: Choco Warbler
rangeDescription: Tropical southwestern colombia (cauca and nariño) to northwestern ecuador
description: Small warbler found in cloud forest in western Colombia and northwestern Ecuador. Field marks include bright yellow underparts a well as dark stripes through face and on sides of crown.

name: Pied Plover
rangeDescription: Riverbanks and mudflats of lowlands to hills in tropical south america east of the andes south to paraguay, south-eastern brazil, and (rarely) north-eastern argentina; west of the andes only in western ecuador
description: Boldly colored shorebird of tropical lowland rivers. Clean black-and-white plumage is distinctive and stands out against its gray wings and orange legs.

name: Chestnut-breasted Quail-thrush
rangeDescription: South-central queensland and adjacent northwestern new south wales
description: Heavily patterned terrestrial bird of western Queensland and northwestern New South Wales. Both sexes have pale eyebrow, gray-brown back, speckled undertail, and black-and-white markings on wing.
